newsitem.title: UK: London bans macabre car and sex film "Crash".
newsitem.headline: London bans macabre car and sex film "Crash".

text.p: Local government officials banned Canadian director David Cronenberg's "Crash" on Wednesday, excluding the film about sado-masochists aroused by car accidents from most of central London's leading cinemas.

The interim ban by Westminster City Council, which covers London's entertainment district, will be reviewed after the British Board of Film Classification (BBFC) has decided whether to allow the film to go on general release throughout Britain, council chairman John Bull said.

Awarded the minor Jury Prize at this year's Cannes film festival for "audacity, daring and originality", "Crash", received a mixed response at its London Film Festival screening. One critic described it as "beyond the depths of depravity".
"The film is sexual but not violent," Cronenberg said.
Westminster coucillors called for three cuts to the film despite protests from over 50 leading film makers.

Cronenberg, best known for the science fiction film "The Fly", starring Jeff Goldblum, described "Crash" as a "strange existentialist romance," and defended it as "experimental and complex, but not a social danger".
Britain's Heritage Secretary Virginia Bottomley disagrees, and has urged local authorities to ban the film even if the BBFC gives it a certificate.
